new_scholarship.selection_notes: SI screens for eligibility, scores eligible applications, then evaluates after the University Admissions announcement. Priority is given to the quality of the application, demonstrated relevant work experience, strong and relevant leadership experience, motivation linked to sustainable development of the applicant's country and region, an approximately equal gender balance and a spread across eligible countries, within the available budget. There are no quotas for specific countries, fields of study or universities. Applicants who also qualify for the Pioneering Women in STEM scholarship are considered under both programmes.

new_scholarship.best_fit: Professionals with several years of work experience and documented leadership experience from one of the 34 eligible ODA countries who intend to use a Swedish master's degree to contribute to the sustainable development of their home country or region.
new_scholarship.notes: The scholarship does not include insurance, grants for family members or the University Admissions application fee, and it does not allow changes to the study programme or extensions of the scholarship period. Applicants for Stockholm School of Economics and Konstfack are handled through separate intakes.

new_scholarship.description: The SI Scholarship for Global Professionals is a Swedish Institute programme for master's studies at Swedish universities, aimed at citizens of 34 eligible countries outside the EU/EEA and Sweden who are liable to pay tuition fees. It is fully funded: SI pays the full tuition fee directly to the university each semester, pays a monthly allowance of SEK 12,000, and makes a one-time travel grant of SEK 15,000 (SEK 10,000 for applicants from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine). Applicants must first secure a place on an eligible English-taught master's programme through University Admissions and then submit a separate SI application in a two-week February window. Scholars join the SI Network for Global Professionals during their studies and the Sweden Alumni Network afterwards.

programme_detail_official.funding_label: Fully funded: 100% of the tuition fee paid directly to the university each semester, SEK 12,000 per month living allowance, and a one-time travel grant of SEK 15,000 (SEK 10,000 for Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine). Not covered: insurance, grants for family members, and the University Admissions application fee.

eligibility: Be a citizen of one of the 34 eligible countries; residence in the country of citizenship is not required
Be liable to pay tuition fees to Swedish universities
Have paid the application fee for master's programmes to University Admissions on time
Apply only to a master's programme listed by SI as eligible for the scholarship, and be admitted or conditionally admitted on the admissions announcement day (reserve places are not eligible)

Demonstrate work experience: applicants from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine must be able to prove work experience; applicants from Bangladesh, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Egypt, Ethiopia, Guatemala, Indonesia, Iraq, Jordan, Kenya, Liberia, Malaysia, Mexico, Morocco, Nigeria, Peru, Philippines, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan, Vietnam and Zambia must have at least 3,000 hours of work experience prior to February 2026, accumulated from a maximum of three employers
Demonstrate leadership experience from a current or previous employer or from civil society engagement
Not be currently enrolled in or hold a degree from a Swedish university or university college
Not have resided in Sweden for cumulatively two years or more prior to the scholarship period
Not have previously been awarded a Swedish Institute scholarship for studies in Sweden
Not hold Swedish or EU/EEA citizenship, a Swedish permanent residence permit, or a work/family-based residence permit tied to a Swedish/EU/EEA citizen
programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: Citizenship of one of 34 eligible countries is required; applicants do not need to reside in that country at the time of application.
programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: Open to non-EU/EEA, non-Swiss citizens of the 34 listed countries who are liable to pay Swedish tuition fees. Exceptions noted by SI: Ukrainian applicants residing in Sweden under the Temporary Protection Directive remain eligible, and Moldovan applicants with dual Romanian citizenship may apply by declaring the eligible Moldovan citizenship.
programme_detail_official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The master's programme must be an English-taught programme on SI's published eligible-programme list for the cycle; eligible fields include Governance, Public Health, Entrepreneurship and Innovation, and STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics).
programme_detail_official.application_method: Submit one scholarship application in the SI online application portal between 9 and 25 February (closing 14:59 CET). The application must be completed in English and must use SI's templates.
programme_detail_official.application_route: Two-stage: apply for an eligible master's programme through University Admissions (universityadmissions.se), obtain the eight-digit application number, then apply in the SI scholarship portal (apply-scholarships.si.se). Stockholm School of Economics and Konstfack applicants follow separate intakes.

programme_detail_official.description: The SI Scholarship for Global Professionals is the Swedish Institute's fully funded master's scholarship for global professionals from 34 eligible countries. It covers the full tuition fee of an eligible English-taught Swedish master's programme, a SEK 12,000 monthly living allowance and a one-time travel grant of SEK 15,000, and includes membership of the SI Network for Global Professionals during the study period and the Sweden Alumni Network afterwards. Applicants must first be admitted to an eligible programme through University Admissions, then submit a separate SI application in a two-week window each February. The scholarship does not cover insurance, grants for family members or the University Admissions application fee, and it does not permit programme changes or extensions.
programme_detail_official.program_type: Fully funded international master's scholarship administered by a Swedish public agency
programme_detail_official.coverage: Tuition fees, monthly living allowance, one-time travel grant and professional network membership; no insurance, no family grants, no application fee.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a citizen of one of the 34 eligible countries and hold no Swedish/EU/EEA citizenship or residence permit
Choose only English-taught master's programmes that appear on SI's eligible-programme list for the cycle (published in mid-November)
Apply through University Admissions and record your eight-digit application number exactly
Pay the University Admissions application fee before the fee deadline
Use SI's 2026/2027 templates for the CV, the work and leadership form and both reference letters
Have the work and leadership form and both reference letters signed and officially stamped, then merge each set into a single PDF
Write the motivation in the portal in English, linking the programme to sustainable development of your country or region
Prepare a passport or national ID photocopy that clearly shows name, citizenship and photo
Submit well before 14:59 CET on 25 February - SI warns the portal is under heavy pressure at the end of the period
common_rejection_risks: Wrong or mistyped eight-digit University Admissions application number
Missing or incorrect SI templates, unsigned or unstamped forms, or multiple documents uploaded where a single merged PDF is required
Declining or changing the admissions result, which removes the application from the running
Only being listed as a reserve or on the waiting list at the admissions announcement
Applying for a programme that is not on SI's eligible list, or to Stockholm School of Economics or Konstfack through the standard route
Missing the University Admissions application or fee deadlines
Not meeting the 3,000-hour work experience requirement where it applies, or not evidencing leadership experience
estimated_uncovered_costs: University Admissions application fee (SEK 900) is not covered by the scholarship
Insurance is not included; SI recommends checking what the host university provides for international students
No grants are provided for family members
The travel grant is not paid to applicants already living in Sweden
document_audit: CV on SI's template, maximum three pages, no additional pages
Work and leadership experience form on SI's template, referee-signed and officially stamped, one single PDF
Two reference letters from two different referees on SI's template, at least one work-based, signed, stamped, one single PDF
Passport or national ID photocopy valid at the time of application
Only the requested documents are accepted; SI does not consider extra documents

alerts.message: The scholarship portal is only open for two weeks in February and closes at 14:59 CET on the final day; no admission is accepted past the deadline.
You are only in the running if you are admitted or conditionally admitted to an eligible programme on the University Admissions announcement day and do not change the result.
The 2026/2027 cycle is closed; amounts and dates for the next cycle are only published in mid-November, so re-check the official page before applying.

submission_workflow: Mid-November: check the eligible-programme list and download SI's current templates
16 October to 15 January: apply for up to four eligible master's programmes at University Admissions and save your eight-digit application number
Late January to mid-February: prepare signed and stamped documents, scan and merge as required
9-25 February: complete and submit one application in the SI portal before 14:59 CET
26 March: check that you are admitted or conditionally admitted to an eligible programme and have not changed your result
By end of April: accept or decline the scholarship offer using the deadline stated in the offer email
